The main takeaway from our work is that
the capacitive loss in GaN devices are much smaller than the turn-on and turn off loss and hence the efficiency of the converter increases with increase in switching frequency.
the capacitive loss in GaN devices is significantly less than in Si devices, and hence GaN devices can operate with a much lower number of devices in a parallel configuration.
the capacitive losses in a GaN based dc-dc converter are significantly less than the losses in a comparable silicon based dc-dc converters.
